metaDescription: Five DEWALT wet-dry vacuums compared by tank size, blower port, battery or corded power and HEPA filtering, from a 0.5 gallon hand vac to a 9 gallon drum.
expertTake: The DEWALT DXV09PA 9 gallon is the best DEWALT wet-dry vacuum for most people: strong 5 peak HP motor, blower port and an upgraded hose. The 6 gallon DXV06P is the smaller, cheaper way into the same family. Skip the corded line if you already own 20V MAX batteries and only need small cleanups, because the cordless 2 gallon units cover that without a cord.
introParagraphs: This guide narrows the field to one maker that sells both corded poly-drum shop vacs and battery models. That makes the choice simple in one way, since the tools share a look and a parts system, and tricky in another, because the names and sizes are easy to confuse.

The real question is corded or cordless, and how big the tank needs to be. A corded drum gives unlimited runtime and a blower port, while a battery unit trades capacity for freedom. Here are five picks, from a hand-held cleaner to a 9 gallon floor machine.

products.name: DEWALT DXV09PA 9 Gallon Wet/Dry Vac with Blower
products.description:
The DXV09PA is the flagship corded poly-drum vacuum in the line. It combines a 9 gallon tank, a 5 peak HP motor and a built-in blower port that can push sawdust and leaves along with extra nozzle adapters. The hose is a revised design that is more durable and flexible than the earlier version, and the 10 ft cord is longer than a typical entry-level unit.

You give up portability for capacity. A 9 gallon poly tank is heavy to lift full, and the machine takes real floor space in a garage. Compared with the 6 gallon DXV06P it holds half again as much and moves a bit more air, but the DXV06P is lighter and costs less. If your cleanups stay under a few gallons, the smaller drum is enough.

In long-term ownership, the rubberized casters and poly tank resist dents and rust. Expect to buy fine dust bags for drywall and sanding work, and a foam sleeve for wet jobs. Replacement filters are easy to find because the line shares filter sizes across its poly models.
products.bestFor: A garage or workshop that needs a large drum and a blower in one machine.
pros: 9 gallon drum covers a full floor cleanup
Built-in blower port clears leaves and sawdust
Flexible upgraded hose is easier to drag
Rubber casters roll smoothly on concrete
cons: Heavy and bulky when full of wet debris
10 ft cord often needs an extension
Paper filter clogs on fine drywall dust

products.name: DEWALT DXV06P 6 Gallon 4 HP Poly Wet/Dry Vac with Blower
products.description:
The DXV06P is the smaller corded poly-drum model, with a 6 gallon tank and a 4 peak HP motor. It is sold as a three-in-one wet, dry and blower machine and is aimed at small cleanup jobs. Rubberized casters swivel smoothly, which makes it easy to pull around a garage.

It gives up capacity and some motor strength to the DXV09PA. At 6 gallons it fills faster on a bigger job, and at 4 peak HP its surge rating is a step lower. In exchange it is lighter, less bulky and a better fit for a home that wants a DEWALT shop vac without the larger footprint.

Ownership is simple: rinse the tank after wet use, wash the foam sleeve and replace the cartridge when airflow drops. The smaller drum dries faster and stores more easily on a shelf. It is a good choice for a car, a deck or a small workshop.
products.bestFor: A home garage that needs a DEWALT shop vac without the bulk.
pros: 6 gallon tank is easy to move and store
Blower function clears debris
Rubberized casters swivel smoothly
Lighter than the 9 gallon models
cons: 4 peak HP is a step down from the 5 peak HP unit

products.name: DEWALT 9 Gallon Poly Wet/Dry Vac, 5 HP, Yellow
products.description:
This 9 gallon poly vacuum uses the same drum size and 5 peak HP motor as the DXV09PA, in the older yellow styling. It is sold for large pick-up jobs in a workshop or on a jobsite, and the rubberized casters swivel easily across rough floors. If you want the capacity without the upgraded hose and extras, this is the plainer option.

The trade is features. The DXV09PA lists a built-in blower port and a newer hose, and this listing leans on the basic drum and motor. Compare the two listings carefully before buying, because DEWALT sells several 9 gallon variants with similar names.

Plan for the usual upkeep: a fine dust bag for drywall, a foam sleeve for wet jobs and a periodic cartridge change. The poly tank does not rust, and the large drum makes emptying a workshop easy. It suits buyers who want proven hardware and a simple layout.
products.bestFor: Jobsites and shops that want a big drum without extras.
pros: 9 gallon tank for large pick-ups
5 peak HP motor matches the flagship
Rubber casters roll over rough floors
Poly tank resists rust and dents
cons: Fewer upgraded features than the DXV09PA

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Cordless 2 Gallon Wet/Dry Shop Vac with HEPA Filter
products.description:
This 20V MAX cordless wet-dry vac holds 2 gallons and uses a HEPA-rated filter that is listed at 99.97 percent efficiency at 0.3 microns. The filter is washable and reusable, which cuts the running cost for the fine-dust work it is designed for. It runs on the same 20V MAX batteries as DEWALT drills and saws.

The tank is small and the motor is limited by a battery, so it is not a floor machine. It is a good match for sanding dust, a workbench or a car, and for a trade user who already carries 20V MAX packs. Compared with the corded DXV09PA it moves less air, but it goes anywhere.

Keep the HEPA filter dry when you can, since HEPA media is fragile when wet. Rinse the washable element gently and let it dry fully. A spare battery makes the difference between a quick tidy and a stalled job.
products.bestFor: Trade users with 20V MAX batteries who need fine-dust capture on the go.
pros: HEPA-rated filter captures fine dust
Washable reusable filter lowers running cost
Uses common 20V MAX batteries
Cordless for cars, benches and ladders
cons: Battery and charger may be sold separately

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Cordless Wet/Dry Hand Vacuum, 0.5 Gallon
products.description:
This hand vacuum is the smallest item here: a half-gallon tank on a 20V MAX battery, with a washable Gore HEPA filter listed at 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns. It has two clean-up modes, a front utility nozzle and an extendable one, and a heavy-duty latch makes it easy to empty.

It is a spot cleaner, not a vacuum for a room. The half-gallon tank fills with a few handfuls of sawdust, and it is not meant for flooded floors. Next to the 2 gallon cordless unit it is far lighter, and it fits in a tool bag.

Keep the filter dry, empty the tank after use and charge the battery before storing. For a bench, a vehicle or a stairwell, it is quicker than hauling a shop vac. A trade user will use it daily, a homeowner a few times a month.
products.bestFor: Quick benchtop, vehicle and stair cleanup on a 20V MAX battery.
pros: Half-gallon tank is easy to carry and empty
Washable HEPA filter captures fine dust
Two nozzle modes reach tight spots
Shares batteries with DEWALT 20V MAX tools
cons: Tiny tank fills in a few minutes
Battery sold separately on some kits

buyingCriteria.explanation: The DEWALT 9 gallon models are corded and run as long as you have a plug, while the 20V MAX units run from batteries and hold 0.5 to 2 gallons. A corded drum moves more air and holds more, and a battery unit goes to a car, ladder or roof. Most owners end up with one of each, and the platform you already own is the deciding factor. Check that the cordless model you want is sold as a kit or a bare tool before comparing totals.

The DXV06P holds 6 gallons, the DXV09PA and its yellow sibling hold 9, and the cordless units hold 2 or 0.5. A larger poly tank is heavier to lift when full of liquid, and a small one needs emptying often. Choose by the biggest spill you expect rather than the average, and remember usable volume is lower than the nameplate.

The DXV09PA and DXV06P include a blower function through the exhaust port, which clears sawdust, leaves and shop dust. Exhaust air is dirty, so remove the filter or keep fine dust out of the drum before you blow. If you already own a leaf blower, you can skip this feature, but it is useful for cleaning shelves.

The two 20V MAX units list HEPA filters that capture 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns, and they are washable. HEPA is only effective if the housing is sealed and the filter is seated. Do not use a wet filter for dry dust, and let a washed filter dry fully. For drywall dust on the corded models, use fine dust bags.

The DXV09PA ships with an upgraded hose that is more flexible than the older one, plus extra nozzle adapters. A stiff hose fights you across a floor, and a poor connector leaks suction. Before you buy, check the diameter and whether the hose locks. A good hose does more for daily use than another peak horsepower. Hose adapters that lock are worth more than a marginal horsepower number.

DEWALT sells several 9 gallon vacuums with similar names, including the DXV09PA and a yellow 9 gallon poly model, and the differences are in hose, blower and accessories. Read the listing for the model number and the feature list. Buying by the picture alone leads to receiving a plainer version than expected.

specDecoder.watchFor: The 9 gallon units hold about half again as much as the 6 gallon DXV06P.

specDecoder.meaning: DEWALT's battery platform name. It is 18V nominal and shares packs across tools.
specDecoder.watchFor: The cordless vacs need a pack and charger if the listing is a bare tool.

specDecoder.meaning: The standard for a HEPA filter. It only applies in a sealed system.
specDecoder.watchFor: Both cordless DEWALT vacs list this, the corded ones do not.

specDecoder.meaning: An exhaust outlet that lets the vac blow air instead of sucking.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DXV09PA and DXV06P have it, the cordless vacs do not.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and tank
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared peak HP ratings and tank sizes across the line. The DXV09PA pairs 5 peak HP with 9 gallons, while the DXV06P pairs 4 peak HP with 6. We treated peak HP as a surge rating and weighted tank size and hose more.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at casters, weight and storage. Rubberized casters appear on the corded poly models, and the hand vac fits in a tool bag. A vac that is hard to move gets used less.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cartridge, bag and HEPA options. The two 20V MAX units list HEPA media at 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns, and the corded units use cartridges. We favored washable filters for running cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed corded power against 20V MAX batteries. A battery unit pairs with existing DEWALT tools, and a corded one gives unlimited runtime. The better pick depends on what you already own.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched blower ports, hoses and accessories to the price tier. The DXV09PA offers the most extras, and the yellow 9 gallon unit is plainer. We called out model-name confusion in each verdict.

rows: Bare tool for owners of 20V packs

cards.label: Corded poly drum
cards.text: The DXV09PA, DXV06P and yellow 9 gallon unit run on a cord with no runtime limit. They hold 6 to 9 gallons and move more air, but they are heavy and tied to an outlet.

cards.label: 20V MAX cordless
cards.text: The 2 gallon HEPA unit and the hand vac use DEWALT batteries. They go anywhere, but the tank is small and runtime depends on the pack.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for a garage floor, and cordless if you move between a van, a ladder and a bench.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 6 to 9 gallon drum, a hose that reaches the bench and a filter that handles fine dust. A cordless unit helps for ladder and bench spots, and a corded one for the floor.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DXV09PA is the best fit for the floor, and the 20V MAX 2 gallon is the best for bench dust. Many shops buy one of each.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use the vac weekly or want the upgraded hose and blower. The DXV09PA is the premium pick, and the HEPA cordless unit pays off for sanding dust.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean up a few times a month. The DXV06P or the hand vac covers that without paying for extras.

maintenance.why: Standing water leaves mildew and a smell. Leave the lid open to dry. A drain plug or a quick tip over a floor drain makes the chore take seconds on the larger drums.
A clogged sleeve cuts airflow. Dry it fully before the next use.
A loaded filter cuts suction. Tap it out outdoors. On drywall and sanding work, swap to a fine dust bag first so the cartridge lasts longer.
HEPA media is fragile. Let it dry completely before refitting.
Heat in a garage shortens battery life. Keep them at room temperature. Charge to roughly half before storing for the winter.

faq.q: Which DEWALT wet-dry vacuum is best for a garage?
faq.a: The DXV09PA 9 gallon is the best fit, with its blower port and upgraded hose. The 6 gallon DXV06P is a lighter alternative if you want a smaller footprint. If your garage floor is cracked or sloped, the rubberized casters on both corded models roll better than hard plastic wheels.

faq.q: Is DEWALT 5 peak HP stronger than 4 peak HP?
faq.a: Only slightly in practice. Peak HP is a surge figure, so the DXV09PA and DXV06P differ more in tank size and hose than in real suction. Compare features, not just the horsepower label.

faq.q: Can DEWALT 20V MAX vacs replace a corded vac?
faq.a: For small jobs, yes. The 2 gallon unit handles sanding dust and spills, but runtime and tank size are limited. For a full garage floor a corded drum is more practical. A second 4.0 Ah pack doubles the working time, and many owners keep one on the charger while using the other.

faq.q: Do DEWALT vacuums have HEPA filters?
faq.a: The two 20V MAX models list HEPA filters at 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns. The corded poly models use standard cartridges. HEPA only works in a sealed system with a seated filter.

faq.q: Can I vacuum water with a DEWALT shop vac?
faq.a: Yes, they are wet-dry machines. Remove the dry cartridge and use a foam sleeve for liquids, and empty the tank afterward. Do not pull water through a paper filter. Rinse the drum soon after a wet job, because a sealed damp tank smells within a day or two.

faq.q: Why are the model names confusing?
faq.a: DEWALT sells several 9 gallon vacuums with similar names, such as the DXV09PA and a yellow 9 gallon poly unit. Check the model number and feature list before buying so you get the blower and hose you expect.
